name: tool-papa-brume-htcxvfcr
description: Conversation preparation — Brume's primary result is a saved card. brume_prepare drafts the card from what the user said, asks them for every fact it would assert, and saves the card with their answers. brume_reset starts a short guided break; brume_complete saves its record when the user says done.
author: Brume

tools.name: brume_prepare
tools.description: Prepare the conversation and save the card — Brume's primary result. Call it in two steps. Step 1: pass `situation` (your faithful relay of what the user said — their words, never additions you invented), the `goal`, `key_point` and `preserve` they stated if they stated them, and your own draft of the card in `draft_opening`, `draft_key_point`, `draft_approach`, `draft_objection`, `draft_response` and `draft_next_step`. The tool returns needs_input with one question per fact your draft asserts — each question masks the value and asks the user to state it — and, when they mention a deadline in the same week with no day, one question about which day to name. Step 2: ask the user every question, then call brume_prepare again with `request_id` and `answers` (one 'id = answer' per question, in the order asked). The tool replaces your values with the user's, saves the card, and returns it. Never write the card's facts yourself — the card's facts are the ones the user stated.

parameters.name: situation
parameters.description: Your faithful relay of what the user said about the upcoming conversation — their words, not additions.

parameters.name: goal
parameters.description: The outcome they said they want, if they said one.

parameters.name: key_point
parameters.description: Their main point, if they stated one.

parameters.name: preserve
parameters.description: A boundary or relationship quality they explicitly want to protect, if stated.

parameters.name: draft_opening
parameters.description: Your draft of the card's opening line — one or two calm sentences.

parameters.name: draft_key_point
parameters.description: Your draft of the card's key point — the one thing they want remembered.

parameters.name: draft_approach
parameters.description: Your draft of the card's approach — how they open the conversation.

parameters.name: draft_objection
parameters.description: Your draft of one hypothetical pushback, for practice.

parameters.name: draft_response
parameters.description: Your draft of how they would answer that pushback.

parameters.name: draft_next_step
parameters.description: Your draft of the card's next step.

parameters.name: request_id
parameters.description: The id the first call returned. Pass it on the second call, with the answers.

parameters.name: answers
parameters.description: The user's answers, one 'id = answer' per question, in the order the questions were asked.

tools.name: brume_reset
tools.description: Optional breathing break, not Brume's result. Start (or continue) a short guided break, rendered verbatim to the user. Before calling, plan it yourself from what the user said: choose `pattern` (cyclic-sigh: 2s in, 1s top-up, 6s out — right before something tense or when keyed up; long-exhale: 4s in, 6s out — a gentle reset between tasks; box: 4s in, 4s hold, 4s out, 4s hold — getting ready for focused work; steady: 5.5s in, 5.5s out — winding down) and `seconds` (60, 90, 120 or 180; 60 if they have little time), and write `title`, `opening`, `cues` and `why`. Describe only the rhythm and how it fits their moment — never effects on the body, brain, stress, sleep or health. The returned script is shown verbatim; do not restate it. If the user asks to change pace mid-break, call again with `pace` and `remaining_seconds` (the plan is kept). When the user says they are done, call brume_complete.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: What the user said they are doing or about to do, as a short phrase. Never invent one.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Breathing pattern you chose.

parameters.name: seconds
parameters.description: Length you chose.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Up to 6 words naming this break.

parameters.name: opening
parameters.description: One or two calm sentences (max 30 words) responding to what they said.

parameters.name: cues
parameters.description: 2–3 short phrases (max 8 words each) about posture or attention, shown during the break. Never counts, timings, or the words in, out, hold, inhale, exhale.

parameters.name: why
parameters.description: One sentence (max 20 words): which part of their note this rhythm fits, describing only the rhythm.

parameters.name: pace
parameters.description: Tempo factor: slow = 1.25x phase length, normal = 1x, fast = 0.8x. Default normal.

parameters.name: remaining_seconds
parameters.description: Deliver only roughly this many more seconds — use when re-invoking to change pace mid-break so the script covers just the remainder (partial cycles allowed). Overrides the planned length.

parameters.name: cycles
parameters.description: Legacy override: exact breath cycles to deliver. Ignored when seconds is given.

tools.name: brume_complete
tools.description: Close out a guided break after the user says they are done. Write `reflection` yourself: at most 2 sentences and 35 words — first acknowledge how it went in plain words (matter-of-fact if they ended early or still feel wired, never guilt), then one concrete next step tied to what they said they are doing next. No emoji, no health claims, and do not mention breathing science. Pass `felt` only if the user said how they feel. The reflection is shown verbatim; do not repeat it. Do not call for abandoned breaks.

parameters.name: felt
parameters.description: Only if the user said how they feel.

parameters.name: reflection
parameters.description: Your closing note, written as described above.
